alternatives.reason: Zero code change, but it binds the product's only model path to one provider and the founder does not hold a Gemini key. The founder holds an Anthropic key with promotional credit and said explicitly that they do not want to be locked into Gemini. A single-provider advisor also means the advisor interface is never exercised by a second implementation, so its provider-neutrality is a claim, not a fact.

The official SDK is the documented default for Go applications, but this module has exactly one dependency (gopkg.in/yaml.v3) and the existing Gemini adapter is already raw net/http. One advisor call per Change version, a fixed request shape and a fixed response shape do not justify a dependency tree; the Messages API contract (POST /v1/messages, x-api-key, anthropic-version, output_config.format json_schema) is small enough to pin in tests. Revisit if the adapter grows streaming, tool use or retries.
Would trade one lock-in for another. The Gemini adapter keeps its behaviour and its UNVERIFIED status; the selection rule treats the two providers symmetrically.

allowed_paths: demo/order-operations-portal/README.md (restore to develop content only; see EB-016 last section)

architecture_impact: The decision advisor is provider-neutral in fact, not only by interface: two model-backed implementations (GeminiAdvisor, AnthropicAdvisor) and the deterministic RuleAdvisor satisfy change.Advisor, and both model adapters send the same user prompt from one function (advisorPrompt). The Anthropic adapter additionally sends a one-line system prompt restating the role and JSON-only rule, and its response schema differs in form (additionalProperties:false on every object, all fields required) because the Messages API requires it. A provider switch therefore changes the model and the provider-specific envelope, not the request, grounding or pricing_ref contract the model is asked about.

Advisor selection moves out of main.go into change.SelectAdvisor(AdvisorConfig): an explicit CONTEXT_RAIL_ADVISOR (rule | gemini | anthropic) wins and must have its key; with no explicit choice, exactly one configured key picks that provider, no key means the rule advisor, and two keys without a choice is a blocked start (exit 2). Silently preferring one provider is the lock-in this record removes, so it is an error rather than a default. This is a behaviour change for an operator whose shell already carries ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for other tools and who relied on GEMINI_API_KEY alone: the server now refuses to start until CONTEXT_RAIL_ADVISOR is set. The blocked exit lives in cmd/context-rail/main.go, which has no tests; the selection rule itself is table-tested in tests/change.

AnthropicAdvisor calls the Messages API over raw net/http with the key in the x-api-key header only, a JSON-schema output format whose pricing_ref enum is the same fixed list the Gemini schema uses, and a 45 s timeout chosen to stay under the HTTP server's 60 s write timeout so the rule fallback can still be written. A refusal stop, a max_tokens stop, a non-200 status, an unparseable body or zero options are all errors; the service then reruns the rule advisor and records an observation, exactly as for Gemini.
Option.advisor_source now takes the value anthropic:<model> as well as gemini:<model> and rule-advisor. No other ledger, Brief or Work Order field changes; the DecisionRecord shape is unchanged.

DR-014's price table (internal/change/pricing.go, GCS storage and egress SKUs for candidate options) is not touched by this decision. The advisor's own API cost is a separate line below; it was never in that table.

The Gemini adapter's behaviour is unchanged; its code now reads the prompt from the shared function and parses into the shared modelProposal type (formerly geminiProposal). Its real-API status stays UNVERIFIED (DR-014, DR-015 unknown 2).
cost_assumptions: One advisor call per evaluated Change version. At Anthropic list price for claude-opus-5-5 (US$4 per million input tokens, US$20 per million output tokens, from the claude-api reference used during implementation; not re-read from the pricing page at decision time) and an estimated 2-3k input tokens (request plus grounding, ten declared documents) and about 1k output tokens, one call is on the order of US$0.03. This is an estimate: the server does not log the usage field and EB-016 did not capture it.

The EB-016 call was paid from the founder's single promotional credit (US$200, expires 2026-11-10 UTC, see the operator notes outside this repo). Any further real calls before that date cost nothing beyond that credit; after it, list price applies unless another credit appears.
Zero cloud spend and zero new dependencies, as DR-015 requires.
unknowns: Whether the Gemini adapter honours the same schema contract against the real API. Still UNVERIFIED; EB-016 is Anthropic-only and the roadmap row says so.
Actual token usage and cost per call. Not measured; a usage log line (counts only, never content) would settle it and is a small follow-up if cost ever matters.
Latency distribution. One measurement (13 s) sits well under the 45 s adapter timeout and the 60 s server write timeout; whether slower requests or larger groundings approach either limit is unknown.

Whether the advisor's candidates are good enough to be worth the call compared with the rule advisor. This record proves access and schema compliance, not quality; a comparison would need the reader test that DR-013 / EB-013 are still blocked on.

The Anthropic API version header (2023-06-01) and the output_config.format shape were taken from the claude-api reference and confirmed by one successful real call; a future API change would surface as an HTTP 400 and a rule-advisor fallback observation, not as a silent change of behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: change.SelectAdvisor exists with the selection rule above and a table test covering: no key, each single key, both keys with and without CONTEXT_RAIL_ADVISOR, an explicit provider without its key, and an unknown provider.

AnthropicAdvisor sends POST /v1/messages with x-api-key and anthropic-version headers, the configured model, and an output_config.format of type json_schema whose schema closes every object with additionalProperties:false and constrains pricing_ref to pricingRefChoices(); tests pin this against an httptest fake and cover the HTTP-error, refusal, max_tokens and zero-option paths.

README.md names both providers and the CONTEXT_RAIL_ADVISOR rule; roadmap.md moves to v1.6 with G1 MET, EB-015 and EB-016 cited, model access stated as shown via go run only, and the Gemini path still marked UNVERIFIED.

EB-016 records one real call through the local go run path: the startup line naming anthropic:<model>, the POST status and duration, a response in which every option's advisor_source is anthropic:<model> and no 'advisor … unavailable' observation appears, and the teardown; the key appears in no file.
go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test -count=1 ./... pass locally with the change set applied; CI is read only if a run is actually seen green.
